Real JVM-backend CORRECTNESS defect on a supported core target: `String.getBytes()` is accepted by the frontend but the JVM backend emits return descriptor `()Ljava/lang/Object;` instead of `()[B` → `NoSuchMethodError`, or `ClassFormatError: Illegal class name ""` when the result is stored. A core codegen bug (JVM is a Stable 1.0 target), so it blocks the RC. Handed to the compiler/JVM lane (no owner in DOING as of 01/10); the launcher masking it as a "JavaFX" error is a neighbouring diagnostic face.

Real JVM-backend CORRECTNESS defect on a supported core target: a `Byte` arithmetic result stays typed `Byte` and the JVM backend emits `Byte.valueOf(int)` without `i2b` narrowing, so a result outside [-128,127] indexes `ByteCache.cache[value+128]` out of bounds and the program crashes (`ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`). Core codegen on a Stable 1.0 target; blocks the RC. Repro `var x = new Byte[4]; b[0]=65; x = b[0] * 256` (expected `16640`, Int promotion). Handed to the compiler/JVM lane (no owner in DOING as of 01/10).

Real JVM-backend correctness defect on the core surface: `String.getBytes()` is accepted by the frontend but the JVM backend emits an invalid call — return descriptor `()Ljava/lang/Object;` instead of `()[B` — so it either throws `NoSuchMethodError` (value ignored) or produces an unverifiable class (`ClassFormatError: Illegal class name ""`) that the launcher masks as a "JavaFX" error. Measured on HEAD (this lane): both reproducers from the issue reproduce exactly. The Kof idiom (`new Byte[n]` + `charAt`) is unaffected; the defect is that the call is accepted and emits invalid bytecode instead of a correct binding or an honest compile-time diagnostic (same family as #156/#147, fixed for `String.format`/`String.replaceAll`). Core JVM surface, must be closed before the first RC.

Real JVM-backend correctness defect on the core surface: `var a: Byte = 120; var b: Byte = 120; var c = a + b` crashes with `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 368 out of bounds for length 256` in `Byte.valueOf`. Root (measured, this lane): `Byte + Byte` is typed `Byte` (`TypeMetrics.commonNumericType`), but the JVM binary-arithmetic path (`JvmOpEmitter.opcodeForArithmetic`) emits `iadd` with no 8-bit narrowing, so boxing passes the untruncated int (240) to `Byte.valueOf` and the cache index overflows; small results (<=127) hide it. Core JVM surface, must be closed before the first RC. Caveat: a naive `i2b`/`i2s` narrow would diverge cross-target (Native `I2B`/`I2S` are unimplemented no-ops), so the fix needs the maintainer's cross-target scope decision.
